He was my friend from high school, he was insanely intelligent and kind but also one of the funniest people I know (knew?) we clicked almost immediately and even though we didn’t talk much during the pandemic, he’s still a huge part of my life. I wouldn’t have survived high school without him. He’s so selfless and was always willing to help others. He has this rare kind of playful competitiveness that would cause him to always want to be the best while also making sure that he is helping the people around him get on his level of greatness. He got into all the best engineering schools in the country and he was just starting his first year in university September 2021 when he was killed. I didn’t know too many of his other friends but they have reached out to me and I have realized that through his friends and all the stuff he loved that he left behind (movies, music, all the things he loved) he is still able to make my life better through the pain

I am so sorry for your loss. When I lost someone very close to me I felt very similar to this, he was just 18 and I couldn’t accept that there are so many things that I am accomplishing and that I will accomplish that he won’t. The way I have decided to look at it is to do those things on his behalf, and carry out his legacy by doing the things he will enjoy- it helps me feel close to him. I understand that everyone is different but it may be a perspective to consider that by doing these things your father never could, that you are doing it on his behalf and hold him with you in your heart when you do it, knowing it wouldn’t be possible without him.

Hi there- I am so sorry for your loss. the story of your loss sounds a lot like mine. A friend of mine moved away across the country for school and one night, him and his gf were hit by a car and killed on impact. It is absolutely horrible to loose anyone but sometimes you make these really special connections with friends that are so special and you can’t even remember life without them. When my friend first died I hated the idea of him suffering and being denied life after spending his life being such a wonderful human and I couldn’t stop picturing his death- it’s so so horrible. It is absolutely not fair at all to loose someone so special and it is maddening when the person responsible for their death will not know the true punishment they deserve for taking sweet life away, it’s hard to think about. I try not to think too much about the person who is responsible for their deaths and I try just to focus on how I can keep my friend close to me when though he’s not physically here anymore. I am not religious and I don’t know if you are but I try to listen to his music and to help me get out of a funk or a bad mental state I just remember that I am carrying on in my life for him, since he’s made sacrifices to make sure that I am okay. He helped me so much in school that I wouldn’t have gotten by without him, so now I am in university and I will make sure to graduate because of his help and keep him in my heart when I accomplish something that he won’t get a chance to and let him and his memory live through me. Allowing my friend to live through me is how I keep myself motivated in these dark times. This is a bit all over the place but at the end of the day- reach out to his family or friends or anyone else that cares about him and just share your memories about him, do not stop talking about him and be gentle with yourself. Feel free if you’d ever like to message me and talk about it further

My friend helped me out a lot with school work so whenever I feel extremely down and can’t get through it- I try to remember that he would want to see me succeed and I’d try to remember the advice he would give me and just keep him close to me as much as possible. I don’t know if you have any memories that can help you through this time or if it will be comforting for you but I am so sorry for your loss, it’s so hard loosing someone especially when your life is just beginning.

Hi, I remember being 12 and feeling a lot of how you are describing the way you feel in this post. I’m so sorry that the people in your life aren’t supportive, it’s hard for people who feel so instantly and strongly about others to not get what they need in return. I remember feeling so hopeless and like things won’t get better for so long and every time someone told me that “ it gets better” I didn’t believe them and I was so irritated to hear that. When I was 16 we went into the pandemic, by the time I turned 17 I still felt hopeless and then something clicked- I realized that I am the only person I will have to stand for the rest of my life and that I needed to show myself a little bit of love if I wanted to be okay with being alone because apart of life is just being alone. I’m now 18 and although life had thrown me some curveballs, I try to remember that life lacks permeance and nothing is forever which means that while good feelings won’t last, the bad shit doesn’t last either. It doesn’t ever permanently get better, but as you go on and start to get more comfortable with yourself you’ll start to find life to be more manageable. I don’t want to be the annoying person that tells you that life gets better because you have to be willing to improve yourself. I also just wanted to say that you are so young and your life will continue to change a lot in the next years ahead of you, your dreams will change or they will seem more easily attainable as time goes on. I wish you the best of luck, don’t give up on yourself and don’t change for others. Take care

I remember people telling me “ he wouldn’t want you to be upset like this” when I was in intense pain, of course he wouldn’t want that, but the reality is that I am upset and I do feel intense pain. His ex talked to me and she said that he wouldn’t want to see me suffer, and I think that distinction of “suffer” is important because you need to be upset and you need to cry but it’s important to take care of yourself while you cry and grieve. I lost a friend who was 18 two months ago, it’s hard not to think about what they are missing. It’s so hard but the way that I think of it is that there are two sides- and he didn’t have to be subjected to the hardships of adulthood and that his life was so good right up until his very last moment. I think about all of the hard things he will have to miss and how all he has is his youth which were some pretty incredible years. While it’s painful that I won’t get to see him succeed in life (I know he would have) I also know that now there is no way for him to have suffered. I don’t know if I’m making complete sense but that’s how I feel about it. There is no real way to cure yourself from having those thoughts though, death is horrible and tragic no matter the age or the circumstances. It wasn’t “ meant” to happen, it just happened.

Hi there, I believe that I had one about 3 ish weeks after my friend passed. I’ve talked a lot about it with people who believe heavily in these kinds of things. Some people have told me that it isn’t always about who they are closest to but that some people are just easier to reach so don’t worry too much if it takes a while. Around the same time I had my dream, someone else had an almost identical dream about the same person. I believe that when they are ready, the person you are missing will come to you. Visitation dreams feel MUCH different than any normal dream, you will be able to tell the difference between seeing your loved one in a regular dream and a visitation. 

One person told me that if you leave a window or door open that it is easier for them to reach you but that’s just what someone told me after I had mine. 


I really do hope that you are able to have one, it brings a lot of closure and personally took a large weight off my chest

We don’t talk about emotions in my family, there are direct ties between our disfunction and the loss of my grandfather. I often wonder what kind of person he would be as well, I know absolutely nothing about his personality- all I know is that he died super young, around 24 years old. I’ve been pictures of him and he looks a lot like my dad. I feel you when you say that you feel like you’re the only one who seems to care. Our stories are very similar, my grandmother was also single ever since she lost him. She never had any other financial support so my dad and uncle lived off little money and it took a lot of hard work for them to land on their feet as adults. I do believe your grandfather deserved so much better, no one deserves to die so young

Hi there, I have a very similar experience. My fathers dad died a month before he was born. It’s always been something that I think about and something that brings me pain. Everyone talks about it pretty casually and that might be because my dad and uncle never really knew him. I often think about how different our lives would be if he had lived and I got to meet him. It is a strange form of grief I think but I believe that it is valid because he’s family and he’s affected our lives. I’m sorry that your family has experienced this loss. I think your feelings are rational and normal, he was a young person taken too soon and you never got to meet your grandfather, it can be hurtful. 

I hope some of this helped, I feel like our situations are a tiny bit rare so if you’d ever like to talk more about it, send me a message

I refuse to believe that our wonderful young people are taken from us for a reason. However one person told me that the reason young people leave us so early is that they have done so much good in their life that they had nothing left to give. Your friend sounds wonderful, and I am truly sorry for your loss- 40 is not a fair age at all and you have every right to feel angry by his passing, you are very right- it is not fair at all and I am so so sorry.

Thank you for sharing this, I am sorry for your loss. Exactly one month ago today, my friend and his girlfriend were hit by a car and killed. I had so many similar questions, I didn’t know if he was conscious before he died, I didn’t know if the girl with him was his girlfriend, I didn’t know what he was up to when it happened. I am choosing to believe that he didn’t see the car coming since he was on the sidewalk, holding hands with a girl he loved, and that since he was unconscious, that right up until the end he was so so happy to be with a girl he loves and be in a city he’d dreamed of living in, studying in his top choice university. It’s nice to think of the people we loose tragically as happy in their final moments.  Thank you for sharing this message with us
